metadata.title: Brief von Lotte Zweig an Hannah Altmann [20. Juni 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.139

## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Lotte Zweig an Hannah Altmann [20. Juni 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.139
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.139
- Datum: 20.6.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 3 Scans

pages.transcription:
c/o Vikingpress
18 East 48th Street
Newyork.

I will write Sunday or Monday after visiting Eva.
Today I enclose two photos, one with Mrs. Sch.
who frowns against the sun. Love, Lotte
20.6.41.

Dear Hanna,
First of all I want to tell you that you better address letters
to us from now on c/o Viking Press, 18 East 48th Street, Newyork, if we
do not cable you another address. For we will probably leave Newyork about
the middle of July and go somewhere to the country because it will be too
hot in Newyork. Up to now we do not yet know where to go and it is every-
where the same trouble: we have no car and so far no one who could do the
house-keeping for us. But we are confident that something will turn up soon,
- don't worry, as one would say here. Today one request. I just received
one of those many enquiries which usually lead to nothing, about the film
rights for "Burning Secret". Unfortunately these rights do not wholly belong
to me as a film has been made seven or eight years ago by a foreign company.
But I had already negotiations about this in London with a refugee lawyer,
Justizrat Rosenberger whose address I unfortunately have not with me. Please
be kind enough to look up our correspondence in the big folder "Films"
which you should find under the heading "Burning Secret-Brennendes Geheimnis"!
I would be very grateful if you could find out his present address and
perhaps you could even cable it to me. I am very, very sceptical if anything
will come out of this vague agent's enquiry, but I would like to have in any
case the possibility to communicate with him.

Just in this moment while I am writing this, I get your cable of
the 19th and thank you very much. You know how much I appreciate Eiseman.
I had only become uncertain because he kept writing me letters announcing
more detailed ones without sending them.

Yesterday we have been for the first time to a concert in the
enormous Lewisohn Stadium. We were at the same table with the son of the
donator of this wonderful gift to the American people, and surrounded by
the big Jewry like the Warburgs, Loebs etc. It was quite interesting as a
contrast to the Schnorrers which are our daily surroundings.

We are confident that you will send us a cable immediately Manfred
has passed his exam, as you know how happy we will be for you both that he
will then have his well-deserved holiday.

Sunday Lotte will go to Croton to see your
little lamb (not more so little now) probably together with
my sister in law and she will give you the usual report.
We are so glad that she feels happy there having all the
funchois {being} at once a child and a kind of mother for
the younger children in the same house, friendly with every
body and especially with her bosom friends Marisa (and
she is already able to have a bosom friend thanks to her
quich devopement into a young lady.) Kindest regards and
love to you all
Stefan

[Randnotiz links:] Lotte is quite well and only so lazy to write.
pages.notes: Brief auf Schreibmaschine geschrieben, mit handschriftlichen Ergänzungen von Lotte Zweig (oben) und Stefan Zweig (unten). Die Randnotiz links ist ebenfalls handschriftlich.
Rückseite des Dokuments, zeigt den durchscheinenden Text der Vorderseite (spiegelverkehrt).

pages.notes: Scan mit Archiv-Farbskala und Grauskala. Der Text ist identisch mit Seite 1, jedoch durch die Skalen teilweise verdeckt.

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar. Die handschriftlichen Ergänzungen von Stefan Zweig am Ende des Briefes sind gut entzifferbar, trotz einiger orthographischer Eigenheiten (z.B. 'funchois', 'quich devopement').
